comparator.name: Bachelor Biomedical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, study-guide, curriculum, learning-line and course pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC biomedical-engineering bachelor. The official study guide assigns 45 EC to free elective space and 15 EC to the Bachelor Final Project; the programme's elective structure also includes a 15-EC USE/ITEC learning line. The remaining 105 EC is compulsory biomedical-engineering formation. The complete 105/15/15/45 allocation is retained below; the official learning-line map and current course pages establish the substance of the compulsory part without requiring unsupported individual-credit reconstruction.

components.name: Compulsory biomedical-engineering programme
components.note: Compulsory formation across biomedical sciences, chemistry, mathematics, physics, programming and biomedical data analysis, biomechanics, biomedical imaging and measurement, biomaterials and tissue engineering, modelling, laboratory skills, challenge-based engineering and professional skills.

components.name: Bachelor Final Project
components.note: The official study guide specifies a 15-ECTS, approximately 420-hour research project completed in a research group.

components.name: USE/ITEC learning line
components.note: Genuine programme choice within the elective part.

components.name: Free elective space
components.note: Genuine 45-EC elective space preserved from the official study guide.

programmes.label: Bachelor Biomedical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology

exception.reason: Biomedical Engineering at TU/e is an integrated engineering-and-life-science degree. Its compulsory formation connects chemistry, cell biology, physiology and pathology with mathematics, physics, programming and biomedical data analysis, biomechanics and mechanobiology, biomedical imaging and measurement, biomaterials and tissue engineering, modelling, laboratory experimentation, challenge-based design and a 15-EC research project. UCR has substantial biomedical science, molecular and cellular biology, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, one life-science laboratory, mathematics, programming, data science, image processing and robotics. It does not offer the required mechanics and biomechanics progression, continuum and material modelling, biomaterials and tissue-engineering sequence, biomedical instrumentation and signal-acquisition laboratories, imaging physics, engineering-design and fabrication progression, staged biomedical laboratory programme or an equivalent 15-EC biomedical-engineering research project. A UCR pathway could form a strong quantitative biomedical-science curriculum, but it would not be a defensible Biomedical Engineering comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official structure accounts for the full 180 EC: 105 EC of compulsory biomedical-engineering study, a 15-EC Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC USE/ITEC learning line and 45 EC of free electives. The official learning-line map and current course pages show that the compulsory programme deliberately integrates molecular and cellular foundations, physiology and disease, chemistry, mathematics, physics, programming and data analysis with biomechanics, imaging, measurement, biomaterials, tissue engineering, modelling and challenge-based projects. Current laboratory education includes chemical-biology skills, cell and biomaterial experimentation, biomedical imaging and data analysis, biomechanics, tissue engineering and cell-based challenges. The final project requires students to formulate, execute and report a small-scale research study in a TU/e research group.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide strong biomedical foundations. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work with blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics support quantitative modelling. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics add programming, analysis, general imaging and computational systems perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no general-physics sequence for biomedical engineering, electromagnetism, mechanics and biomechanics progression, stress-strain and constitutive modelling of biological tissue, biomaterials, mechanobiology, tissue engineering or biofabrication, biomedical sensors and instrumentation, physiological signal-acquisition laboratory, optical and medical-imaging physics, biomedical device-design studio, or advanced experimental sequence integrating cells, materials and engineered systems. DISDATA212 concerns general digital image processing rather than image formation, measurement hardware and biomedical imaging laboratories. HCBLIFE214 is one introductory life-science laboratory and cannot replace the target's staged chemical-biology, cell-material, biomechanics, imaging and tissue-engineering practical formation. The workbook also has no 15-EC biomedical-engineering research project. UCR's closest combination therefore covers biomedical and computational foundations while leaving the target programme's defining mechanics, materials, instrumentation, experimental-engineering and capstone spine unmatched.
